# Natural Family Planning

**Authors:** Sharon Sung, Beverly A. Mikes, Aaron Abramovitz

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Natural family planning is the use of fertility awareness to either prevent or achieve pregnancy. In the United States, approximately 1% of women use natural family planning methods for contraception. In contrast, its global use is about 3.6%. There are numerous options available to individuals and couples who desire family planning. Natural family planning is unique because it can be utilized both as a conceptive and contraceptive method and has no inherent adverse effects. As a contraceptive option, natural family planning has a typical failure rate of 22% to 24%. Effectiveness may be misrepresented as it is directly related to patient education, personal commitment to the method, menstrual cycle regularity, and the ability to abstain from intercourse during peak fertility. High-quality women's health involves meeting patients' reproductive intentions, offering a wide variety of options, and reducing contraceptive failure.
